items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to employee-owned enterprises; to amend the cooperative corporations law, in relation to creating an advisory panel on the viability of increasing employee-owned enterprises; and to amend the tax law, in relation to a capital gains exemption
items.lawCode: Amd §3032, Ed L; add §95, Coop Corps L; amd §612, Tax L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5349            REVISED MEMO 04/28/2017

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
employee-owned enterprises; to amend the cooperative corporations law,
in relation to creating an advisory panel on the viability of
increasing employee-owned enterprises; and to amend the tax law, in
relation to a capital gains exemption

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

  THIS BILL WILL PROVIDE BUSINESS AND INDUSTRY TRAINING TO MEMBERS OF
AN EMPLOYEE-OWNED ENTERPRISE, CREATE AN ADVISORY PANEL THAT WILL
EXPLORE THE VIABILITY OF INCREASING EMPLOYEE-OWNED ENTERPRISES IN THE
STATE, AND PROVIDE A 100% CAPITAL GAINS EXEMPTION FOR THE SALE OF
STOCK TO AN EMPLOYEE-OWNED ENTERPRISE.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 amends paragraph (a) of subdivision 4 of section 3032 of the
education law to include training that will promote the successful
management and/or operation of employee-owned enterprises.

Section 2 amends the cooperative corporations law by adding a new
section 95, which creates an advisory panel on the viability of
increasing employee-owned enterprises in the State.

Section 3 amends subsection (c) of section 612 of the tax law by
adding a new paragraph 42, which provides a 100% capital gains
exemption for the sale of stock to an employee-owned enterprise.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Employee-owned enterprises benefit New York State and its citizens.
They provide stability and staying power for local jobs- they are far
less likely to move out of state, or even out of the local region,
because of the connection that employees have in the area in which
they work and live. It is imperative that we ensure their continued
existence and growth.

With the wave of business-owners reaching retirement age, many
employees fear that they may lose their job or have to relocate when a
business owner retires and sells their company. This bill provides
that retiring business owners may sell their company back to their
employees without incurring a tax on the sale, which could affect the
number of jobs and families that stay here in New York State.

Ultimately, this bill will strengthen the local economies of New York
State, and support local small businesses.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016: A9618

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :

To be determined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5349A

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the economic development law, in
relation to establishing an advisory panel on employee-owned
enterprises within the division of small business services; and
providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof

 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :

This bill would create an advisory panel on employee-owned enterprises
in order to report and make recommendations on how best to support
such businesses and promote the formation and growth of new
employee-owned enterprises in New York State.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

This bill would establish an advisory panel within the Department of
Economic Development for the purpose of reviewing state laws and
programs in order to report and make recommendations on how to support
and promote employee-owned enterprises in New York State.  The panel
would consist of twelve members with expertise related to
employee-owned enterprises, including the Commissioners of Economic
Development, Labor, and Tax and Finance.

The panel would be responsible for identifying and recommending
strategies to promote the creation and development of new
employee-owned enterprises, evaluating state and local programs
intended to support such businesses, and recommending new or
underutilized methods of supporting such businesses, among other
things.

The panel would also be required to issue a report no later than
September 30, 2018 with its findings.

 DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE) :

The original scope of the bill was narrowed to focus on creating an
advisory panel.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Employee-owned enterprises provide stability and staying power for
local jobs. Employee-owned enterprises are far less likely to move out
of state, or even out of the local region, because of the roots the
employees of these enterprises have in the areas they work and live.
Studies have found that wages, sales, productivity, and retirement
plans for employee-owned enterprises are higher than those of
comparable, privately owned corporations. As an increasing number of
small business owners reach retirement, many employees fear they may
lose their job or have to relocate when a small business owner retires
and sells their company.

This bill would ensure that New York State is taking proactive steps
to support and promote employee-owned enterprises, which would
preserve local jobs, encourage new innovative business strategies that
benefit workers, and invest in local communities.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill in 2017.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :

Undetermined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediate.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 26 Chapter 435
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 5349-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the economic development law, in relation to estab-
        lishing  an  advisory panel on employee-owned enterprises within
        the division of small business services; and providing  for  the
        repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This  bill  would  create an Employee Owned Business Advisory Panel to
review state laws and programs impacting employee-owned business  enter-
prises,  and  to make recommendations further supporting their formation
and growth.
 
  Employee-owned enterprises are an exciting and creative component of a
diverse economy. New York's economy is powered by the diversity  of  its
businesses,  and  the proposed Advisory Panel will help grow and support
this industry. To ensure that the Advisory Panel has sufficient time and
expertise to complete its mandate, I have secured an agreement with  the
Legislature  to  pass legislation in the upcoming session that addresses
these concerns. On that basis, I am signing this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                      (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                                ______

summary: Relates to establishing an advisory panel on employee-owned enterprises; provides such panel shall consist of twelve members who shall report and make recommendations on how best to support existing employee-owned enterprises and promote new employee-owned enterprises.
